Seminar Title:

Dietary Advanced Lipoxidation End Products (ALEs) shorten lifespan and induce Sarcopenic obesity in Drosophila melanogaster

Seminar Type:

Departmental Seminar

Department:

Life Science

Speaker Name:

Lokanath Mishra

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

LS Seminar Hall

Date and Time:

09 Nov 2026 3:30 PM

Contact:

7008772552

Abstract:

Advanced Lipoxidation End Products (ALEs) play a key role in the progression of neurodegenerative diseases, but their role in aging and other pathophysiological conditions is underexplored. The role of ALEs was checked in obesity and muscle degeneration. BSA and Oleic acid were mixed and stored at 37 °C for 42 days, with periodic UV exposure, to produce ALEs. Then it is fed to D. melanogaster, a well-known model organism used to decode muscle degeneration and obesity. A series of changes was observed in ALE-fed flies: they were obese, and their glucose concentration was comparatively higher. The belly was swollen, and the lipid droplets in the gut were higher. Climbing and jumping abilities were lower, whereas LDH activity was higher. In ALE-fed flies, the cell death in the muscle was higher, and the actin filaments and septate junctions were disrupted. The Reactive oxygen species (ROS), nitric acid Species (NOs), and Lipid peroxidation were higher in ALE-fed flies. The mRNA expression level of Relish and InR was upregulated, whereas the genes Myosin Heavy Chain (Mhc), Act88F, Tm1 and Sallimus were downregulated. From the study, it was concluded that exogenous ALE ingestion leads to decreased lifespan and sarcopenic obesity.
